rationale: Re-running my four probes against codex 4eb0bb8f confirms every finding I raised is fixed — the unpushed local-base commit now survives instead of being orphaned, an offline completion cleans and lands on an explicitly non-synced local base, wipe-issue with an unreachable origin succeeds again exactly as the baseline a98c04b3 does, and the discard is logged before the reset so it survives a later checkout failure — while the per-clone completion semantics (eligible clone cleaned, ambiguous clone refused untouched) are better than my own pin's batch abort, with typecheck clean and 28 focused tests passing; the one residual is that a clean clone whose local base carries unpushed commits now makes non-force wipe refuse where the baseline silently reset it, which I judge an acceptable fail-closed trade because it names both remedies and changes nothing, though checking out that local base where it stands rather than refusing would clean the clone and preserve the commit.
